c.tagline: Golden pagodas rise above colonial streets and river haze.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered; negotiate fare before departure or use the Grab app for a fixed upfront price.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; many hotels and tour operators keep direct lines to private clinics. Tourist Police available in central Yangon.

avoid.reason: Steer clear of any protest gatherings, military installations and checkpoints given post-2021 political instability, and skip the outlying industrial townships, which offer nothing for visitors and see more crime.
Street crime has risen since the coup, so take extra care after dark, during power cuts, and with bags around Bogyoke Market and busy downtown streets.

hood_desc: Colonial-era downtown grid around Sule Pagoda with crumbling heritage architecture, street markets, and budget-to-luxury hotels; best for first-time visitors who want to walk to major sights.
Dense, atmospheric Chinatown/Latha area famous for night food markets on 19th Street; suits budget travelers and foodies who don't mind noise and crowds.
Leafy, upscale residential area around Shwedagon Pagoda and Golden Valley with embassies and colonial mansions; suits travelers wanting quiet, greenery, and proximity to Myanmar's most sacred site.
Lakeside district around Kandawgyi (Royal) Lake with resort-style hotels, parks, and skyline views; good for mid-range/upscale travelers wanting a scenic, less chaotic base.
Quiet, leafy area around Inya Lake popular with diplomats and NGO staff, dotted with lakeside hotels and cafes; suits longer-stay visitors and those wanting calm over convenience.

water.note: Tap water isn't treated to safe standards; stick to bottled or boiled water and avoid ice from unknown sources.

transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash (small kyat notes) directly to the conductor on board; the circular train ticket is bought in cash at station windows. There is no unified transit card, so carry small MMK bills.
transit.hours: Buses and trains generally run approx. 5am-9pm; limited night options, most travelers use Grab or taxis after dark.
transit.note: YBS bus routes are extensive but signage is mostly in Burmese; the circular train is a scenic 3-hour loop popular with tourists rather than a fast commuter option.

train: Myanmar Railways intercity trains to Mandalay, Bagan, Bago
bus: Long-distance buses from Aung Mingalar and Dagon Ayeyar bus terminals
ferry: Dala Ferry across the Yangon River

transit.m: YBS airport shuttle bus (Yangon Airport Bus, ~45-60 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not traditionally expected but small tips for good service (guides, drivers, porters) are increasingly welcomed, especially in tourist-oriented businesses.

food.name: Mohinga

places.name: Rangoon Tea House

places.name: Kosan Street (Yaw Min Gyi area)

places.name: Rangoon Tea House

places.name: Aung Thukha

landmarks: Shwedagon Pagoda
This colossal gold-plated stupa, said to enshrine relics of the Buddha, glows above the city skyline and is Myanmar's most sacred and photographed site.
Sule Pagoda
Standing at the literal center of downtown traffic circles, this 2,000-year-old golden stupa has long served as both spiritual landmark and city navigation point.
Botataung Pagoda
Unique for its hollow interior lined with mirrors and gold leaf, this riverside pagoda lets visitors walk through its glittering core, unlike most solid stupas.
Chaukhtatgyi Buddha Temple
Home to an enormous 65-meter reclining Buddha with intricately painted glass-mosaic soles, this temple is a must-see for its scale and craftsmanship.
Karaweik Hall
This ornate concrete replica of a royal barge floats on Kandawgyi Lake, its shimmering golden mythical bird design making it one of Yangon's most photographed sights.
Bogyoke Aung San Market
This sprawling colonial-era covered market is packed with jade, gems, handicrafts, and antiques, offering an atmospheric dive into Yangon's trading culture.
Yangon City Hall
A masterpiece of Burmese architectural fusion, this grand colonial-era building blends traditional Burmese roof tiers with European civic design near Sule Pagoda.
Colonial Downtown Yangon
Lined with crumbling yet grand British-era buildings, downtown Yangon's streets are a photographer's paradise of faded colonial grandeur and street life.
Kandawgyi Lake
This scenic lake with a boardwalk framing views of the Shwedagon Pagoda's reflection is a favorite spot for sunset walks and leisurely photography.
Maha Wizaya Pagoda
Built to commemorate Myanmar's Buddhist heritage, this pagoda near Shwedagon features a beautifully painted dome ceiling depicting celestial and zodiac scenes.

dom.op: Myanmar Railways — tickets at Yangon Central Station, no online booking

train.note: Myanmar has no international train connections. Domestically, Myanmar Railways runs from Yangon Central Station (notably the overnight Yangon-Mandalay line and the Yangon circular railway), but tickets are sold in person at the station, not online. Expect slow, basic service.

bus.note: No reliable international coach. The overland border to Thailand at Myawaddy-Mae Sot has been largely closed to foreign travellers amid the ongoing civil conflict as of 2026, so check current status carefully. Domestic express coaches (e.g. JJ Express) run from Yangon's Aung Mingalar highway bus terminal to Mandalay, Bagan and beyond.

ferry.note: No international ferries. Domestic Inland Water Transport (IWT) river boats sail the Irrawaddy (e.g. Mandalay-Bagan), and the short Yangon-Dala cross-river ferry runs from Pansodan jetty.
